set.approach: Park at the Fireside area just off Highway 1A west of Banff and follow the trail across the creek. Go straight at the first junction (the left fork is signed for Cory Pass) onto the Edith Pass trail, and at the next signed junction about an hour on, take the Cory Pass trail. The trail rises easily through trees beneath the south and centre summits of Mount Edith; after a brief drop you reach scree under Edith's north summit and Mount Louis. Pick across the boulders and take the faint path that rises to the foot of the south face. Two short corners show at the foot of the face; the left one has an appealing crack, but the route takes the right one, marked by a single bolt. The start lies roughly below the big corner that forms the crux of the fifth pitch.
set.descent_text: The route finishes on the summit ridge, a short exposed walk to the summit cross. From the summit, the way down is a rappel descent on the north side of the peak, starting at a bolted anchor above a gentle gully. Rappel the gully on bolted anchors until it steepens, then walk up the short, easy ramp on climber's left that follows the last of those rappels; an earlier ramp is a common wrong turn. More rappels from the top of that ramp lead to a ledge, a short walk along it reaches the next station on the wall, and further rappels end on easy ground. A steep trail then drops to the foot of the mountain near the start of the Gmoser Route. Rock shoes are workable for the descent.

review.notes: Approach and start from the route page and area page; descent from the area page (peak rappel descent) plus the route page note that the descent is doable in rock shoes. No rappel count given.

set.approach: Park at the Fireside area just off Highway 1A west of Banff and follow the trail across the creek. Go straight at the first junction (the left fork is signed for Cory Pass) onto the Edith Pass trail, and at the next signed junction about an hour on, take the Cory Pass trail. The trail rises easily through trees beneath the south and centre summits of Mount Edith; after a brief drop you reach scree under Edith's north summit and Mount Louis. Pick across the boulders and take the faint path that rises to the foot of the south face. A trail then runs right, below the east ridge. At the fork keep left for this route (the right branch continues to Homage to the Spider) and climb to the base of the cliff. Three scoops sit low on the northeast face; the route starts roughly below the rightmost one and works up and left through the middle one. Rope up near the fork rather than at the base, since the descent does not return there.
set.descent_text: The route reaches the summit cross by the ridge crest. From the summit, the way down is a rappel descent on the north side of the peak, starting at a bolted anchor above a gentle gully. Rappel the gully on bolted anchors until it steepens, then walk up the short, easy ramp on climber's left that follows the last of those rappels; an earlier ramp is a common wrong turn. More rappels from the top of that ramp lead to a ledge, a short walk along it reaches the next station on the wall, and further rappels end on easy ground. A steep trail then drops to the foot of the mountain near the start of the Gmoser Route. Rock shoes are workable for the descent.

review.notes: Approach from the route page (fork, three scoops) and area page; descent is the peak rappel descent from the area page.

set.approach: Park at the Fireside area just off Highway 1A west of Banff and follow the trail across the creek. Go straight at the first junction (the left fork is signed for Cory Pass) onto the Edith Pass trail, and at the next signed junction about an hour on, take the Cory Pass trail. The trail rises easily through trees beneath the south and centre summits of Mount Edith; after a brief drop you reach scree under Edith's north summit and Mount Louis. Pick across the boulders and take the faint path that rises to the foot of the south face. A trail traverses right below the east ridge to a fork; stay right here (the left branch is the Kain Route). Follow it to a rise that sits down and left of the line, then scramble up to roughly the height of the corner system, then cross a gully by an exposed traverse to the right to reach the base, where a belay bolt marks the start. Leave anything you are not carrying up at the base, because the descent does not come back to it.

review.notes: Approach and the leave-gear-at-base fact from the route page; descent from the area page.

set.approach: Park at the Fireside area just off Highway 1A west of Banff and follow the trail across the creek. Go straight at the first junction (the left fork is signed for Cory Pass) onto the Edith Pass trail, and at the next signed junction about an hour on, take the Cory Pass trail. The trail rises easily through trees beneath the south and centre summits of Mount Edith; after a brief drop you reach scree under Edith's north summit and Mount Louis. Pick across the boulders and take the faint path that rises to the foot of the south face. The route starts right of the Gmoser Route, on slabs below and to the right of a chimney.

review.notes: Start location and the join with the Kain Route from the route page; summit descent from the area page. Medium: the descent is the peak descent, not stated on the route page itself.

set.approach: Two trails reach the upper cliffs of Castle Mountain. The fire lookout trail leaves Highway 1A west of Castle Junction, passes the lookout, then climbs to a break in the headwall and on to a small hut on Goat Plateau. The Rockbound Lake trail leaves near Castle Junction and arrives on the plateau at Eisenhower Tower. From the hut, follow the trail east along the foot of the cliff; Brewer Buttress is the last buttress before the tower, and a belay bolt in a bay on its right side marks the start. From the tower, follow the plateau trail across to the same bay.
set.descent_text: Descent is by rappelling a line of fixed anchors that follows the crest of the buttress. From the top, walk about 50 m east along the ledge and look for cairns that mark the first rappel; a single ring bolt on a large block set back from the edge gives access to that station. The first rappels go straight down, and lower down the line stays on the prow of the ridge, so avoid drifting into the side gullies.

review.notes: Approach from route page and area page (both approaches). Descent from the route page rappel section; rappel count and lengths left out.

set.approach: Take the Rockbound Lake trail from the trailhead just east of Castle Junction on Highway 1A. Once the trail has levelled off, turn left onto the cairned climber's trail through trees, which steepens at the cliff bands and then follows a narrow, exposed ledge system from right to left. A cairn marks a steep scramble up a wall and a gully, probably class 3 or 4, to the top of the cliff band, and a trail from there leads to the base of the tower. The climb begins at the left end of the Dragon's Back, a small buttress jutting from the tower's foot, via a short chimney or gully to a bolted rappel anchor.
set.descent_text: Descend by rappelling the left variation of the face. Bolted anchors, with some easy downclimbing between them, lead down the upper rib to the scree bowl; cross the bowl and traverse right to the anchor where the two variations part. More rappels reach the station over the short wall at the junction of the Dragon's Back and the tower, and the wall and the gully east of it are rappelled to the ground close to the start of the route, so approach shoes can be left there.

review.notes: Approach from the area page Rockbound Lake approach and the route page; descent is the route page descent. No counts given.

set.approach: From the fire lookout, take the left-hand trail across the foot of the cliffs. It passes the turn-off for the hut access gully, crosses a large drainage and then about two more scree drainages, with trails on either side to aim for and one rock step at about third class. Keep following the good trail along the cliff edge, watching for bolts on the wall. The start is at a very low bolt with two more to its left, beside a wide crack that is easy to recognise, with the Castles in the Sky prow visible on your right. If the trail fades, you have gone too far.
set.descent_text: From the top of the lower tier, walk climber's left towards the hut, continue left past it and follow cairns down to the foot of the cliff. Alternatively, keep climbing to the top of Brewer Buttress and leave by the descent gully, the second huge gully along, which involves rappels.

review.notes: Approach and descent both from the route page; the lookout trail from the area page.

set.approach: Climb to the hut on Goat Plateau by the fire lookout trail from Highway 1A. From the hut, walk towards Bass Buttress and Kraut Pinnacle and follow the trail to the left side of the pinnacle. The first pitch is the conspicuous crack that leans left, roughly 15 m short of where Blue Sky Days starts.

review.notes: Approach only; the route page gives no descent.

ab_castle_mountain_lookout_buttress.skip_reason: route page has no approach or descent text (only a note that a published topo is wrong)

set.approach: Hike through Paradise Valley to Lake Annette, pass around the lake's right-hand shore and angle up to the toe of the buttress that separates the north face from the Sphinx face. A short cliff band guards the face; find a gap in it and climb one brief pitch at low fifth class to reach easier ground.
set.descent_text: From the top of the buttress, slog loose scree on the glacier's left side to the crest of the ridge, where the East Ridge route arrives above the Black Towers. Continue along the corniced summit ridge to the top, then descend the easy southwest slopes to Moraine Lake. A long walk along the Moraine Lake road returns to the Lake Annette trailhead.

review.notes: Approach and descent are both on the route page.

set.approach: From the Paradise Valley trailhead, hike up the valley and around Lake Annette, past the starts of Greenwood-Jones and the Sphinx face. Continue up steep scree nearly to the notch beneath the Aemmer Couloir, then trend uphill on dirty ledges into an obvious gully that rises to the right. Scramble the gully to a big scree ledge, turn left and walk to where the roped climbing begins.
set.descent_text: The buttress leads to the upper East Ridge, below the Black Towers, and the route continues up the towers to the summit ice cap and the summit. Descend the southwest ridge to Sentinel Pass, drop north into Paradise Valley and follow the trail signs back to the trailhead.

review.notes: Approach and descent from the route page.

set.descent_text: Descend by downclimbing the route. Rappels can be set up where needed: at the rock step on the ridge, just below that step, and over the bergschrund at the foot of the black band of rock.

review.notes: Descent only; the route page begins its approach at the start of the glacier with no trailhead, so no approach written.

set.approach: Walk the Arnica Lake trail towards Twin Lakes, on the Banff and Kootenay border just east of Mount Stanley. At the lower of the Twin Lakes (the third lake on the way in), follow its west bank, choosing a line through trees and brush to the tarn below the southeast cirque. From the tarn, cross meadowy ridges and talus to reach the east ridge itself, which is broad and split by gullies.

review.notes: Approach only; the route page offers two descents but says one is untested, so no descent written.

set.approach: The route starts at the col between Mount Whyte and Devil's Thumb, reached above Lake Agnes. From the col, scramble up talus on climber's left into a small basin that gives access to the east ridge, then follow the ridge.
set.descent_text: A short steep wall just below the summit is the hardest step. Descend the north ridge to the col between Whyte and Mount Niblock, then pick a way down through the cliff bands back to Lake Agnes.

review.notes: Both from the route page. Lake Agnes link to the col is implied by the page (round trip from the lake).

set.approach: From the large Moraine Lake parking lot, head east to the Consolation Lakes trail. Follow it past a creek, then take a well-trodden climber's path branching right and pick a line over talus and later scree to a prominent horizontal ledge about 30 m above the true toe of the feature. Walk about 40 m along the well-worn trail on the ledge; the route starts where further travel would become more exposed, by the last significant tree.
set.descent_text: From the top, follow large cairns in a southeasterly direction and climb through a steep wall at its shortest point (about 5.2). Keep the same heading to a trail trending south-southwest to a small col. A steep, loose gully with a trail that improves as you go leads down to the start of the horizontal ledge.

review.notes: Area page and route page agree on the ledge approach; descent is the route page.

set.approach: From the Moraine Lake parking area, follow the Consolation Lakes trail to the north shore of the southern Consolation Lake, then ascend the giant scree slope to the foot of the wall. The line starts left of a big gully and works up corners and faces to the summit of a large detached pillar beneath the obvious wide crack near the top of the wall.
set.descent_text: Go down the north ridge from the summit, all the way to the Tower of Babel's descent gully. Expect it to be slow and involves some downclimbing, rappels off single-bolt anchors and plenty of scree.

review.notes: Both from the route page; Consolation Lakes trail from the area page.

set.approach: Hike from Moraine Lake up to Wenkchemna Pass, where Neptuak's northwest ridge ends. Either take the ridge straight from the pass, up broken ledges and big holds to an easy chimney, or cross snow to the left and climb steeply up and right to meet the ridge where it is low angled.
set.descent_text: Descend by retracing the ridge. Getting down to the Neptuak-Deltaform col takes care, and some parties rappel parts of it. Lower down, a steep gully or recess can hold snow or ice.

review.notes: Approach from area page and route page; descent is reverse of route per the route page.

set.descent_text: Three descents are possible. One traverses behind Tuzo and Allen and goes down the Schiesser Route to Moraine Lake. Another follows the glacier on the back side, weaves down the cliff bands to the lake below and leaves by the Tokumn Creek trail, which is long and not maintained throughout. The third continues over the summit of Deltaform, reverses the northwest ridge over Neptuak and descends to the pass, using fixed rappel anchors and a lot of exposed downclimbing.

review.notes: Descent only; approach given only as a start location on the face, no trail from the road. Distance of the Tokumn route left out (one source).

set.approach: From the parking lot, take the Cavell Meadows trail and then head up the moraines to the foot of the east ridge. The scramble to the base is loose and unpleasant, especially in the dark. A snow couloir flanks the ridge on one side and the north face on the other.
set.descent_text: Most parties reverse the route by downclimbing. The alternative is to continue over the summit and down the west ridge, a much larger traverse that stays on the ridge until the col with Mount Sorrow, because dropping off sooner can lead into cliff bands, and which ends in the Tonquin Valley.

review.notes: Both from the route page. Bear note and times left out.

set.descent_text: From the summit, descend the southeast ridge to a rappel anchor on a slung block, then continue down the ridge, bypassing difficulties mostly on the right. At the col between Colin and the next peak to the south, follow cairned scree down to a creek bed and follow it down to the hut.

review.notes: Descent only; approach on the route page starts at the Hawk-Colin col with no trail from the road. Rappel length left out.

set.approach: Leave the Wates-Gibson hut on the clear trail heading south to the moraine. Climb the moraine's steep nose on its trail until the path dies out, angle up and right, then cut back left to a broad grassy bench. Traverse the bench onto the ridge and scramble along the crest to the foot of the first of three towers; if the crest looks hard, go left.
set.descent_text: The buttress leads onto the ridge crest. Scramble along the ridge to Outpost Peak's summit, then drop south to the Outpost-Memorial saddle, crossing the top of the glacier and avoiding crevasses. Scramble the east ridge of Memorial to its summit, descend steeply and scramble down its southwest ridge, then follow the moraine back to the hut.

review.notes: Both from the route page. Times left out.

set.approach: Park at the gravel pit off the David Thompson Highway near Saskatchewan Crossing, walk north and cross the creek wherever it is easiest. To dodge heavy bushwhacking, go about 50 m north into the forest, then smash east uphill parallel to the highway until you hit a small, intermittently flagged trail. Follow it, taking right branches, to the drainage on the east side of the tower and follow that up. At the top, traverse west and up the next-to-last ledge below the cliff base, walk along the base to the notch in the dark limestone bands and scramble up to a flat area at the foot of the prow. The start is the right-facing corner right of the big roof.
set.descent_text: Walk off east towards the top of the drainage used on the approach. Most of it is class 2 scrambling with one brief class 4 downclimb, and crossing farther east before the drainage narrows may avoid it. Finish down the drainage until the trail reappears below the regrowth.

review.notes: Approach from area page and route page; descent from route page.

set.approach: Start from a pullout on the Icefields Parkway's east side, roughly 12 km north of the icefields. Ford the river and look for the yellow sign marking the trail, then follow a narrow trail on the south side of the valley for two hours or so, then turn west up a scree gully and cross Woolley Shoulder. The Lloyd MacKay hut is visible from there at the north end of Little Alberta. From the hut, traverse snow slopes and scree, keeping your elevation, until you arrive beneath the northeast ridge.
set.descent_text: Descend by the Japanese Route. From the summit, follow the ridge south through a notch and a couple of short rappels to a deeper notch and the main rappel gully, then make a long series of rappels down it to the yellow rock ledge. Traverse the ledge to two more rappels, one of them overhanging, then work down choss gullies, scree and a cliff band, following cairns, to the snow under the east face. Cross the valley floor and climb the ledges below Little Alberta back to the hut. The descent is hard to find in the dark.

review.notes: Approach from the area page and route page; descent from the route page. Rappel counts left out (single source).
